content.overview: Irrigation-water pH and alkalinity are related but different. pH describes hydrogen-ion activity at the moment of measurement; alkalinity describes the water's acid-neutralizing capacity, largely from bicarbonates/carbonates. Repeated irrigation can therefore influence root-zone pH even when the incoming water pH alone looks unremarkable.

vocabulary.definition: The acid-neutralizing capacity of water, commonly expressed as calcium-carbonate equivalents.
A dissolved carbonate species that often contributes to irrigation-water alkalinity.
Resistance of a solution to pH change when acid or base is added.

sections.title: pH is not alkalinity
sections.body: Extension guidance emphasizes that a pH measurement alone does not reveal acid-neutralizing capacity. Water can have relatively high pH with modest alkalinity or have alkalinity that materially influences media pH over time.

sections.title: Repeated inputs matter
sections.body: Bicarbonate/carbonate load is delivered repeatedly with irrigation, so cumulative effect depends on alkalinity, irrigation volume, substrate buffering and fertilizer reaction rather than one reading.

sections.title: Treatment decisions require measurement
sections.body: Do not select acidification or water-treatment intensity from pH alone. Measure alkalinity and verify any treatment against qualified safety and equipment controls.

workedExamples: Two source waters at similar pH can have different alkalinity and therefore different long-term effects on media pH.
A grower repeatedly lowering reservoir pH without measuring alkalinity may be treating a number rather than understanding buffering load.
commonMistakes: Using pH as a synonym for alkalinity.
Assuming one reservoir adjustment predicts root-zone behavior for the whole crop.
Applying water-treatment chemistry without validated measurement and qualified controls.
content.practicalApplication: Include source-water pH and alkalinity in the same test panel and trend root-zone pH over time to determine whether buffering is influencing the crop system.
content.summary: pH tells you current acidity/basicity; alkalinity tells you how strongly water can resist acid and influence root-zone pH over repeated irrigation.
